facts.statement: Hsisosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform that lived in China.
facts.quote: Hsisosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform from China.

facts.statement: Hsisosuchus was likely a medium-sized predator reaching about 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: It is likely to have been a medium-sized (~3 m long) predator.

facts.statement: Fossils of the species H. chungkingensis were discovered in the Shangshaximiao Formation near Chongqing city.
facts.quote: Fossils of H. chungkingensis were found in the Shangshaximiao Formation (near Chongqing city).

facts.statement: The species H. dashanpuensis was found in the Xiashaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: H. dashanpuensis was found in the Xiashaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The species H. chowi was found in the Shangshaximiao Formation.
facts.quote: H. chowi was found in the Shangshaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype of H. chowi includes a nearly complete skull measuring 25 cm long, along with mandibles, most of the vertebral column, and many other skeletal parts.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen consists of a nearly complete skull (25 cm long), mandibles, most of the vertebral column, partial pectoral and pelvic girdles, most of the forelimbs, fragments of hindlimbs and many osteoderms.

facts.statement: Hsisosuchus is classified within the family Hsisosuchidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Hsisosuchus as belonging to the parent group Shartegosuchidae.
Hsisosuchus fossils date to the Middle and Late Jurassic periods.
Hsisosuchus lived between the Bajocian and Tithonian stages, approximately 170.9 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Tithonian (170.9 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Hsisosuchus was described by Young and Chow in 1953.
The authority for the genus Hsisosuchus is Young & Chow, 1953.
